The '''2018–19 Scottish Premiership''' (known as the '''[[Ladbrokes]] Premiership''' for sponsorship reasons) was the sixth season of the [[Scottish Premiership]], the highest division of [[Football in Scotland|Scottish football]]. The fixtures were published on 15 June 2018 and the season began on 4 August 2018.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/201819-fixture-release-day-confirmed/ | title=2018/19 fixture release day confirmed | publisher=[[Scottish Professional Football League|SPFL]] | date=26 April 2018 | access-date=26 April 2018}}</ref>

Twelve teams contested the league: [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] and [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].

On 4 May 2019, Celtic won their eighth consecutive title and 50th overall after a 3&ndash;0 win over Aberdeen.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48075065|title=Aberdeen 0–3 Celtic: Neil Lennon's side secure eighth consecutive Scottish title|date=4 May 2019|publisher=BBC|access-date=4 May 2019|first=Tom|last=English}}</ref>

==Teams==

'''To Premiership'''

[[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] secured the [[2017–18 Scottish Championship|Championship]] title and promotion to the Premiership on 14 April 2018 after a goalless draw with [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43678697 |title=St Mirren 0–0 Livingston |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=14 April 2018 |access-date=14 April 2018}}</ref> who were also promoted after winning the [[2017–18 Scottish Premiership#Final|play-off final]].<ref name="play-offs">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44097532 |title=Partick Thistle 0–1 Livingston (agg 1–3) |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=20 May 2018 |access-date=20 May 2018}}</ref>

'''To [[2018–19 Scottish Championship|Championship]]'''

[[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] were relegated to the Championship on 12 May 2018 after a 1–1 draw with [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44013678 |title=St Johnstone 1–1 Ross County |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=12 May 2018 |access-date=12 May 2018}}</ref> [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] were also relegated following a 3–1 aggregate defeat to Livingston in the play-off final.<ref name="play-offs"/>

==Format==
In the initial phase of the season, the 12 teams will play a round-robin tournament whereby each team plays each one of the other teams three times. After 33 games, the league splits into two sections of six teams, with each team playing every other team in their section once. The league attempts to balance the fixture list so that teams in the same section have played each other twice at home and twice away, but sometimes this is impossible. A total of 228 matches will be played, with 38 matches played by each team.

===Matches 34–38===
After 33 matches, the league splits into two sections of six teams i.e. the top six and the bottom six, with the teams playing every other team in their section once (either at home or away). The exact matches are determined by the position of the teams in the league table at the time of the split.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47825342|title=Scottish Premiership: Rangers host Celtic in second last game after split|work=BBC Sport|date=5 April 2019|access-date=5 April 2019}}</ref>

==Premiership play-offs==
The quarter-final was contested by [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] and [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], with Inverness Caledonian Thistle advancing to the semi-final where they lost to [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]. Dundee United faced [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in the final, with the Saints securing the last place in the [[2019–20 Scottish Premiership|2019–20 Premiership]] after victory in a penalty shoot-out.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/spfl-play-offs|title=SPFL play-offs|date=4 May 2019|publisher=SPFL|access-date=4 May 2019}}</ref>

==Broadcasting==

=== Live Matches ===
The SPFL allows Sky Sports and BT Sport to broadcast up to six live home matches (combined) for each club, although this is only four for Celtic and Rangers. The TV deal allows the broadcasters to show 30 games each (and the play-offs for BT Sport) and provides approximately £21m to the SPFL per season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/spfl-strike-new-tv-deal-6419830|title=SPFL strike TV deal with Sky and BT for Premiership and Play Off coverage|last=Kyle|first=Gregor|date=2015-09-10|work=dailyrecord|access-date=2017-08-15}}</ref>

=== Highlights ===
Sky Sports hold the rights to Saturday night highlights and show the Premiership goals on [[Sky Sports News]] in their ''Goals Express'' programme. Gaelic-language channel [[BBC Alba]] can broadcast in full the repeat of 38 Saturday 3pm matches "as live" at 5.30pm. The main Premiership highlights programme is [[BBC Scotland]]'s ''[[Sportscene]]'' programme, which shows in-depth highlights of all six Premiership matches every weekend. [[STV (TV channel)|STV]] show the goals on Monday nights during the Sport section of their ''News at Six'' programme. The SPFL also uploads the goals from every Premiership match onto its [[YouTube]] channel — available from 6pm on a Sunday for UK and Ireland viewers and 10pm on a Saturday for those worldwide.
